source: Interfaces Magazine issue 20, "Can you tell the difference?" by Jakub Krehel: a 27-question A/B quiz with answers. Questions 23, 25 and 27 are knowledge questions, so 24 items are visual. The media are not in git (no licence to copy them): pass their folder with --media.
split: Fixed before any model run. Items are sorted by question within the two kinds (still, motion) and alternate tune, held-out, so each half holds 5 stills and 7 motion items. Tuning reads only the tune half.
layout: Each poster and clip shows option 1 on the left half and option 2 on the right, above an answer bar. An option's input is its half, cut above barTop (poster pixels; clips are half size), with its number badge painted over. A clip option is a strip of frames from its window (seconds). "same" gives both options the whole frame, for a clip that never shows the other state.
visible: false marks an item whose media never show the difference the question tests (decided from the clips before any model run). Those items stay in the count.

items.differs: Heading text-wrap balance and description text-wrap pretty against default wrapping.
Negative letter-spacing on the large heading against default spacing.
Curly quotes and one ellipsis character against straight quotes and three periods.
A gradient interpolated in oklch against sRGB, which goes muddy grey in the middle.
Avatars with a subtle outline beside a bordered Invite button against avatars without one.
A card over a map with a layered transparent shadow against a solid border.
Outer radius 20px (12px card plus 8px padding) against other values. The clip never moves the slider off 4px.
20px padding on the icon side of a button against an even 24px.
A phone page sized with h-dvh, whose bottom button shows, against h-screen, which hides it.
Inputs with a focus ring against outline-none with no replacement. The clip focuses only option 1.
A running timer and lap list with tabular-nums against proportional digits.
A popover that scales from the corner by its trigger against one that scales from its center.
A dropdown that opens from scale(0.95) against one from scale(0.3).
A copy button that swaps its icon and keeps its label against one that changes the label to Copied! and its width.
A nav dropdown that animates its height and shifts content 8px in the direction of travel against one that snaps.
A drill-down menu that slides in from the right on open and the left on back against one that does not.
A CSS transition that reverses when interrupted against a keyframe animation that snaps. The clip never interrupts it.
A search input focus with a 300ms subtle spring against a 600ms bouncy one.
A panel exit over 70% of its width with opacity and blur against a full slide. The clip shows only the open.
Calendar day hover that changes color instantly against a 500ms fade. The clip hovers only option 1.
Toolbar tooltips that show at once while moving between buttons against ones that wait each time. No tooltip shows in the clip.
A moving square animated with transform, which runs smoothly, against left, which stutters.
A 24px moving button with a 44px pseudo-element hit area against one whose hit area is its size. A hit area has no pixels.
With reduced motion on, a toast that keeps its fade and drops the slide against one that drops all animation.
